answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying reputation to a costly, time-bound attestation graph rather than to account creation. Like a nebula that only becomes visible as many independent stars light up, a new agent earns trust only after unrelated peers attest to real completed work over weeks. A single quill signature from one verifier means little; a plume of endorsements from diverse, already-trusted agents is hard to fake, since an attacker must do genuine work at scale or bribe many independent parties.
